headline: AI goes public and claims discoveries, while the walls go up
summary: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, so a frontier lab is now graded by the market every trading day, and Gary Marcus already argues the stock is crashing. The same week, AI claims moved from code to discovery: an Anthropic mathematician says he and Claude found a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, still unverified, and Isomorphic is working with Merck on a new cancer drug. METR's update adds the caveat: capability keeps compounding, but judgment still trails coding. Meanwhile the walls are going up, as Signal blocks screenshots from OS-level agents and OpenAI moves against distillation that copies models without their safeguards. Your move: hand agents the measurable work, keep judgment with your people, and audit what your agents can see and where your models come from.

threads.title: Graded every trading day
threads.line: Anthropic is public now, so lab strategy gets a daily market verdict. Expect louder bulls, louder bears and faster narrative swings.

threads.title: From coder to discoverer
threads.line: Labs now pitch AI on math, physics and drugs. Treat each claim as unverified until checked, but watch where they land.

threads.title: The walls go up
threads.line: Apps block agents, labs fight copying and providers get compromised. Know what your agents can see and where your models come from.

threads.title: A model for every job
threads.line: Gemini 4 Neon joined the lineup and production teams switch fast. Assign models by task and price every merged PR.

threads.title: Who owns the workday
threads.line: Microsoft, Perplexity and now Apple want to be the agent your people work through. Choose on purpose before habits choose for you.
